messages.author: de4fa02b71eb4cce
messages.subject: QTLBIM concerns
parts:
Hello all,

I have some concerns about QTLBIM. I have a RIL population which I read in as a BC (I read on here that qtlbim will not recognize "riself"). 

  • The first concern I have is that I need to treat "RIL" as a random factor; however, when I look at the output of my qb.data() it seems to have an issue with this. It reports RILs "0 - 163"; however, it is actually 1-164. 
  • The second issue I have concerns how qtlbim interprets "NAs". The output of my qb.data() replaces my NAs with "999.0000" (in my read.cross() statement I stated what NAs were and it read it correctly in that step). I don't know if this truly is the breeding value it interprets, but I couldn't find any documents that discussed this. 
  • Next, when using qb.best() I get strange warnings about "1: In `levels<-`(`*tmp*`, value = c("1", "1", "2", "2", "3",  ... : duplicated levels will not be allowed in factors anymore".  
  • Finally, when I use qb.best() the qtl that are printed out all have the exact same loci if they are on the same chromosome.  For example, when the "best pattern" suggests 2 qtl on chromosome 1 the summary statement says that both qtl are at locus 27.7390.  This is true for all chromosomes regardless of the number of qtl.
I hope that I am being clear here, I have run models using stepwiseqtl(); however, my final QTL model extremely large and I am stuck with a model selection problem.  Thus, I wanted to embark down the QTLBIM methods so I could fit qtl, qtl x e, and qtl x qtl interactions all at once. 

Thanks,
Kyle
